title: Pulse-pressure reserve failed an all-record cross-hospital CAD prediction test; missingness explained most apparent harm
abstract: Fixed models trained in 294 Budapest patients were transferred to 200 VA Long Beach patients. Adding exercise pulse-pressure reserve beyond noninvasive risk/exercise measures and pressure components worsened log loss from 0.980160 to 1.015899 (difference +0.035739; conditional 95% interval +0.024575 to +0.047888; joint source/target refit interval -0.007124 to +0.064066). The 139 complete-pressure records showed essentially no change (-0.000298; conditional interval -0.004417 to +0.003857). Missingness was 1/294 versus 61/200. A missingness-only feature reproduced most apparent harm; an exploratory no-added-indicator ablation reduced the difference to +0.005261. This all-record audit substantially overlaps prior SCI diastolic-rise work, with no biomarker novelty claimed. Independent recruiting institutions supplied the datasets, but global linkage is unavailable. Author self-checks and clean offline reruns were completed. No incremental utility or physiological harm is established.
